name: Eggplant
lede: Eggplant is a dark greyish purple named for the fruit of *Solanum melongena*, which British English calls the aubergine.

sections.title: A fruit's name
sections.body: The Pigment Compendium notes that the aubergine (eggplant), *Solanum melongena*, is one of about 1,700 species in the genus *Solanum*, which also includes the potato [1]. A relative, black nightshade, has berries that are green, turning purplish to black when ripe, and an old recipe uses its juice to make a green writing ink [1]. The immature berries and foliage are toxic [1].

sections.title: Aubergine in China
sections.body: Paterson records that Ming-era porcelain called *wu t'sai*, Five Colours, was decorated in apple green, aubergine, iron red, violet and yellow [2].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch derives from ISCC-NBS block 230 (1955), the Maerz and Paul dictionary, the xkcd survey and the Crayola list [3]. The nearest ISCC-NBS name is "dark grayish purple", 5.7 units away [3]. It sits near [[plum]], [[puce]] and [[mauve]], and darker than all three.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: It appears in 40 of 23,781 archive paintings, 0.17 per cent, rarer than 60 per cent of named colors [4]. Inside a painting it is most often a hidden color, in 52 per cent of the 23 paintings where it counts [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 0.4 per cent of 1,674 paintings, 2.8 times the museums' baseline [4]. The earliest dated example is Ambrogio Lorenzetti's, from 1337, though the early archive is thin and that is a floor [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings [4].
